# Topic reference

**Generated by `scripts/clause-library/build-topic-reference.py`. Don't edit by hand.** Every subject the clause library covers, one entry per `topic_key`, grouped the way a lease is. A new state answers every topic here (SOP rules 27 and 36): a clause, an education row (including a confirmed absence), or a recorded reason the topic doesn't apply. The questions under a topic are things earlier states found worth checking; they are prompts, not a complete list.

364 topics from 13578 active rows across 56 states. "Rows in N states" counts states with any row on the topic.

To add a topic, write a row with a new `topic_key`. To add a question, list it under "Proposed topic questions" in the state log; Claude Code adds it here at sync.

(California: Cal. Const., art. XV, § 1, sets the rate 'upon the loan or forbearance of any money, goods, or things in action, or on accounts after demand' at '7 percent per annum', and lets 'the parties to any loan or forbearance' 'contract in writing' for up to '10 percent per annum' where the money is 'for use primarily for personal, family, or household purposes'. The section doesn't name rent or leases, so whether a lease's charge on overdue rent is a 'forbearance' is a question for case law.
